skill.name: gh-stack
skill.description: Use for stacked PRs with the gh-stack extension: creating, viewing, editing, pushing, submitting, syncing, rebasing, merging, or checking out a stack, or splitting multi-part work into reviewable layers. Also use whenever a stack is checked out or the user mentions stacks, branch layers, or dependent PRs.
skill.summary: Manage linear stacks of dependent GitHub pull requests with reliable, non-interactive gh-stack workflows.
skill.author: jssblck

content.user_title: Manage Stacked Pull Requests with gh-stack
content.value_statement: Dependent pull requests are difficult to organize, update, and merge safely. This skill guides reliable gh-stack workflows for linear branch stacks.
actual_capabilities: Plans linear branch layers before implementation.
Creates and extends stacks with explicit branch names.
Submits branches as linked draft or open pull requests.
Synchronizes local branches with GitHub stack state.
Rebases dependent branches and guides conflict recovery.
Checks out, inspects, unlinks, and merges stack scopes.
limitations: Supports only linear stacks with one parent and at most one child.
Requires GitHub CLI and the gh-stack extension.
Cannot reorder or remove layers non-interactively.
Relies on repository permissions and stacked pull request availability.

use_cases.title: Split a feature for review
use_cases.description: Plan backend, interface, and test changes as ordered pull requests with focused diffs.

use_cases.title: Maintain an active stack
use_cases.description: Update a lower layer, rebase dependent branches, and synchronize remote pull requests.

use_cases.title: Recover a disrupted workflow
use_cases.description: Diagnose divergence, rebase conflicts, locked state, or interrupted stack modification.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect the current stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect my current gh-stack state and summarize each branch, pull request, and required action.

prompt_templates.title: Plan feature layers
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a gh-stack for [feature]. Separate concerns into reviewable branches and explain their bottom-to-top dependency order.

prompt_templates.title: Update a lower layer
prompt_templates.prompt: Move [change] into its owning branch, commit it, rebase every dependent layer, and verify the resulting stack.

prompt_templates.title: Recover and merge safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose [stack problem], preserve existing branches and pull requests, recover non-interactively, then merge only [target scope] after verification.

output_examples.input: Plan a stack for authentication, API routes, and interface integration.
output_examples.output: Create authentication first, API routes second, and interface integration last. Each pull request depends only on reviewed lower layers.

output_examples.input: A lower branch changed and every branch above now needs rebasing.
output: Check out the lower branch and commit the focused change.
Rebase the branches above it, resolve conflicts, and return to the top.
Push the stack and verify each pull request.

output_examples.input: Local and GitHub stack structures have diverged.
output_examples.output: Compare both chains, choose the authoritative structure, unlink only the incorrect grouping, then rebuild without deleting branches or pull requests.

best_practices: Create the stack before editing files and keep one concern in each layer.
Use explicit remote names and non-interactive flags for agent workflows.
Inspect machine-readable stack state before and after mutating operations.
anti_patterns: Do not implement everything on one branch and split it afterward.
Do not commit a lower layer concern on the top branch.
Do not run interactive stack commands in unattended agent sessions.

faq.question: What is a stacked pull request?
faq.answer: It is one pull request in an ordered branch chain, based on the branch directly below it.

faq.question: Does this skill install gh-stack?
faq.answer: It provides the installation command, but GitHub CLI access and installation permissions must already be available.

faq.question: Can it manage multiple remotes?
faq.answer: Yes. Mutating commands need an explicit remote or a configured default push remote.

faq.question: Can it reorder stack layers automatically?
faq.answer: No. Non-interactive reordering requires unlinking the stack, correcting Git ancestry, and initializing the stack again.

faq.question: How are rebase conflicts handled?
faq.answer: The skill identifies exit code three, guides conflict resolution, and supports continuing or aborting the stack rebase.

faq.question: Does merging always bypass repository rules?
faq.answer: No. Repository requirements and merge queues still control whether and how pull requests merge.
